active_themes.label: Confirmation Under Duress
active_themes.summary: Warsh confirmation remains on track procedurally, but today's headlines about Fed rate-hike odds jumping expose the real issue: markets are now openly pricing the possibility that the Fed will be pushed toward tighter policy by political pressure rather than data. This is not about Warsh as a person. It is about what his confirmation signals if it happens while Powell faces Trump pressure and the Iran crisis deepens—a capitulation that destroys Fed independence as a credible institution.

active_themes.label: Iran Escalation Test
active_themes.summary: Iran seized a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, the most direct challenge to US authority since the ceasefire extension. Oil traders remain oddly unmoved (WTI below $95), suggesting markets still expect negotiated resolution. But the cost is showing up elsewhere: UK 30-year gilt yields hit 28-year highs, Australian inflation expectations are rising, and BofA explicitly warns the war threatens the two pillars of US growth (AI capex and consumer spending). The test is whether the next escalation breaks the market's 3-week negotiation assumption and reprices to months of supply disruption.

active_themes.label: Decisions Made Under Threat
active_themes.summary: The pattern has a new data point: Apple cut its high-yield savings account rate by 15 basis points, joining the collapse of federal Grad PLUS loan access. These are not isolated moves—they are the observable output of lenders de-risking at the institutional level. When every major financial institution moves in the same direction simultaneously (reducing consumer credit exposure), it signals fear of downstream default risk. That fear is being driven by energy-shock inflation expectations, not by actual employment weakness yet.

active_themes.label: Credit Access Narrowing
active_themes.summary: Apple Card savings rate cut and federal student loan program collapse are now confirmed data points showing lenders retreating. Student loan borrowers are forced into private alternatives at higher cost and shorter terms. This is the setup mechanism for a consumer spending shock—not happening yet, but positioned to happen if employment weakens or if inflation expectations stay elevated long enough to force real wage compression.

open_watchlist.condition: Fed official (Powell, governor, or staff) makes public statement on rates that sounds politically motivated rather than data-driven
open_watchlist.meaning: First explicit signal that institutional capture has moved from theory to practice; would likely trigger equities sell-off and 10-year yield spike.

open_watchlist.condition: Senate Democrats signal willingness to vote against Warsh confirmation (not delay, but actual opposition votes above 10 senators)
open_watchlist.meaning: Would slow timeline and force Warsh to make explicit commitments on Fed independence; could delay confirmation into June and create window where market reprices the regime shift risk.

open_watchlist.condition: Iran announces official negotiating delegation with specific names and mandate statement within 48 hours
open_watchlist.meaning: Confirms talks are moving from ceasefire extension to actual negotiation; opens door to 3-6 week resolution timeline instead of indefinite blockade.

open_watchlist.condition: WTI oil closes above $100 for two consecutive trading days
open_watchlist.meaning: Signals market no longer believes Iran talks will hold; reprices blockade duration from temporary to structural; forces stagflation repricing in equities.

open_watchlist.condition: Powell makes public statement acknowledging Trump's May timeline or hinting at stepping down
open_watchlist.meaning: Confirms Fed leadership is being rewritten under political pressure during active crisis; market reprices institutional credibility and Fed independence premium disappears.

open_watchlist.condition: 10-year Treasury yield rises above 4.2% while S&P 500 stays flat or declines
open_watchlist.meaning: Signals market is pricing inflation or institutional risk premium (not growth), indicating dual crisis is being repriced as stagflation rather than contained geopolitical shock.

open_watchlist.condition: Fed official makes public statement on rates that references Trump, politics, or May timeline
open_watchlist.meaning: Confirms that Fed independence is now conditional on political acceptance; investors begin reducing duration exposure and repricing long-end yields on credibility discount.

open_watchlist.condition: Powell or any Fed governor makes public statement referencing Trump, May timeline, or political considerations in policy context
open_watchlist.meaning: This triggers immediate market interpretation of Fed capitulation, unanchors inflation expectations, and signals the end of Fed independence as a credible constraint on policy.

open_watchlist.condition: Another major non-bank lender (Capital One, Discover, American Express savings product) cuts savings rates within 7 days
open_watchlist.meaning: This confirms the credit-pullback pattern is institutional, not idiosyncratic, and signals lenders expect material wage compression from inflation within 6-9 months.

open_watchlist.condition: 10-year Treasury yield breaks 4.3% while S&P 500 remains flat or declines
open_watchlist.meaning: This signals real inflation expectations are rising and equities are repricing higher discount rates; the AI/tech narrative cannot overcome inflation-shock fundamentals.
